subject: sea krait
title: Venomous Sea Snakes Hunt in Gangs, and Fish Wait for Their Leftovers

scenes.text: Fish on this reef have nowhere to hide. Not even inside the rock.
Off Lombok, Indonesia, divers keep seeing venomous sea kraits hunting together. One dive counted twenty-one.
The snakes move in tight groups, less than two metres apart.
The front snakes slide into cracks in the reef. The others wait outside for anything that bolts.
Then trevally follow the snakes, ready to snap up whatever escapes.
So a fish hiding in a crack has two choices. Stay with the snake, or run into the trevally.

description:
Divers off southern Lombok, Indonesia, recorded Erabu sea kraits hunting communally on 52 occasions, with up to 21 snakes seen on one dive.
Snakes probe reef crevices while others wait outside, and bluefin trevally and emperor fish follow along to catch escaping prey (Scientific Reports, 2023).
Which hunter would you rather face, the snake or the fish?
first_comment: Scientists still haven't measured how much the teamwork helps, only that it keeps happening. What other animals do you think hunt as a team?
